classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the equal legs formed by a square’s diagonal, solve the resulting repeated-square equation and interpret nearest-millimetre precision.

content.prompt: A parent is asked to make some scarves for the local Scout troop. Two scarves can be made from one square piece of material by cutting on the diagonal. If this diagonal side length is to be 100 cm long, what must be the side length of the square piece of material to the nearest mm?

answer.worked:
$s$ centimetres is the side length of the square. Its diagonal is $100\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}s^2+s^2&=100^2\\2s^2&=10000\\s^2&=5000\\s&=\sqrt{5000}\text{ cm}\\s&\approx70.7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
To the nearest millimetre, the side length is $707\text{ mm}$, or $70.7\text{ cm}$.
